body:
OBSERVED by Myk's claude.ai session on 2026-08-17, driving the live MCP connector: roughly one call in
four failed, four failures across the session, every one recovering on an immediate retry with an
identical payload. Error text: `this connector's server hostname doesn't resolve or isn't reachable
from this network`. The same behaviour was seen in a PRIOR session, so it predates that day's
connector work.

WHAT IT IS NOT, established rather than assumed:
- Not the store. The failures never reached it.
- Not the debugging proxy that sat in front of the store that evening: its request log recorded ZERO
  upstream errors across the whole session, and the behaviour predates the proxy's existence.
- Not payload-dependent. The identical payload succeeded on retry.

SO THE FAILURE IS UPSTREAM OF THE STORE: name resolution of the Tailscale Funnel hostname
(`*.ts.net`) from Anthropic's side, or the funnel ingress refusing a connection under whatever
condition produces that message. Loam cannot fix a resolver it does not run. What Loam CAN own is
that an integrator reading that message debugs the wrong thing — it names a misconfiguration when the
truth is a transient.

WHY IT IS WORTH A TICKET ANYWAY: any client that polls a Loam store reached through a funnel sees
this, and the store's own documentation is where an operator will look first. The deliverable is
therefore documentation and, if a retry surface exists on our side of any hop, a retry.

THE WORK:
1. MEASURE IT HONESTLY FIRST. A loop of N identical calls through the public URL, recording the
   failure rate and the exact error, from a vantage point that is not the host itself (the host may
   resolve the name by a different path than the internet does). Without a measured rate this is
   hearsay; one-in-four is a session impression, not a number.
2. Determine which hop fails: resolution of the `.ts.net` name, or the funnel relay's connection. A
   long-running resolver probe against the public name distinguishes them.
3. If it is the funnel, say so in the operator-facing docs where `--public-url` is explained: a
   funnelled store is reached through a relay whose transient failures present to clients as a
   hostname problem, and a polling client should retry once before reporting a misconfiguration.
4. Consider whether a store reached this way should be documented as needing a stable ingress (a real
   DNS name and a terminator the operator runs) for anything an integrator depends on.

RAILS: a measured before/after failure rate is the evidence; there is no unit rail for someone else's
resolver. If step 3 lands documentation only, its rail is the docs test that the `--public-url`
guidance names the transient.

NOT A LOAM DEFECT until step 2 says otherwise. File the finding, keep the honesty.
title: The connector's hostname fails to resolve on roughly one call in four, and it reads as a misconfiguration
